question.text: Which of the following BEST describes a relative-value style strategy used by Category III AIFs?

answer.text: A convertible arbitrage strategy that takes a long position in a company's convertible securities and a simultaneous short position in the equity shares of the same company
A buy-and-hold strategy that only invests in IPOs and holds the allotted shares until they are listed
A pure cash strategy that invests only in overnight money-market instruments without any other exposure
A dividend-capture strategy that only buys high-dividend stocks just before record date and exits the next day

explanation.text: The Logic: Relative-value style strategies seek to profit from pricing relationships between related securities rather than from outright directional moves in the market. Convertible arbitrage, as described in the cited workbook chapter, is a classic example: a Category III AIF takes a long position in a company's convertible securities and at the same time a short position in the equity shares of the same company, so that the position is structured around the relationship between the two instruments rather than pure long-only exposure. The Trap: A buy-and-hold-only IPO strategy is essentially a directional, long-only approach to new issues and does not exploit a relative-value relationship. A pure overnight cash strategy carries no relative-value structure. A pure dividend-capture trade is event-driven on a single security, not a relative-value structure built around the pricing relationship between two related instruments of the same issuer. Note: The cited workbook chapter explicitly discusses convertible arbitrage as a Category III strategy and uses the LTCM example to illustrate relative-value convergence trades in sovereign bonds. Listing "pairs trading" and "statistical arbitrage" by name as the canonical relative-value strategies is not supported in the cited pages; the framing above instead anchors the relative-value concept on the workbook's convertible-arbitrage description and general industry knowledge.
